text:
alex: Customer report — Android app streaming stopped mid-response after switching from carrier to a phone hotspot, then enabling a corporate VPN. They got partial JSON then stream closed. Customer worried about being billed for partial output.

maria: Can you paste the client logs and the approximate duration when this happened? thread id from the app?

alex: Here are the logs the customer sent (redacted):

```
2024-11-02T14:22:03.341Z INFO connect to sse
2024-11-02T14:22:05.802Z INFO receiving chunks: {"id":"msg-123","chunk":"..."}
2024-11-02T14:22:06.100Z WARN network switch detected: wlan0 -> ap0
2024-11-02T14:22:06.450Z INFO vpn starting
2024-11-02T14:22:06.460Z ERROR stream aborted: ECONNRESET
```

alex: They said it was about ~3s after hotspot attach and immediate VPN start.

jeff: Did they have re-auth or token rotate around that time? token TTL race can close connection if code requests refresh and swaps Authorization header mid-stream.

alex: Customer checked — token not refreshed. They call SSE with the same token.

maria: Could be NAT/port rebind + VPN tunnel teardown closing the TCP session. Need packet capture or server-side connection logs. @eng-runtime-bot any SRE traces for that session id?

eng-runtime-bot: Received request: id msg-123, remote ip 18.205.45.12 -> closed at 2024-11-02T14:22:06.463Z with RST from client side. No server-side error logged.

sara: Thanks, that supports client-side reset. Two likely failure modes: 1) client OS aggressively kills socket when NATT mapping changes; 2) VPN client does user-space network stack switch triggering RSTs. Mobile hotspots often change IPs/ports quickly.

tim: Quick repro suggestion for support: ask customer to reproduce with `adb logcat` and with `tcpdump` on the phone tethering host (if possible). Also ask whether they can reproduce without VPN.

alex: I sent repro steps: 1) start streaming on cellular 2) enable phone hotspot and tether a laptop 3) start VPN on phone 4) observe SSE behavior. Provided snippet for curl-based SSE test for engineering: 

```
# on laptop tethered to phone hotspot
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-x" 
```

jeff: Engineering note — runtime has a 30s keepalive but short bursts will still see graceful close if TCP RST. We should consider adding a lightweight application-layer ping to detect midstream rebinds earlier and attempt reconnection/resume semantics.

maria: For billing: because the server sent partial chunks and then connection closed by client RST, billing should only include tokens the model emitted (we meter server tokens at emission). I'll confirm with billing but this should not be double-charged.

alex: Customer asked for a workaround — suggested toggling `Connection: keep-alive` and enabling client-side retry with idempotent resume where possible. Also suggested pause/resume on network change.

sara: I'll open an eng-runtime ticket to investigate detect-and-resume for transient mobile handoffs. @jeff can you add a short design doc?

jeff: Will do. Creating doc and will include metrics we can capture: RST rate on mobile ip-change, average resume success, token-charge reconciliation scenario.

alex: Customer happy for now with workaround and note about billing. I'll follow up with logs if they reproduce. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — keeping this thread open until eng has a proposal.
_comment: This document is a single Slack thread (root + replies) in the support channel. Messages are in chronological order and prefixed with sender names.
